## What can you actually run?

A critical distinction: battery capacity (Wh) tells you how long you can run something; inverter output (W) determines what you can run at once.

| RV appliance | Typical power |
|---|---:|
| LED lights | 10–50W |
| Laptop and phones | 30–100W |
| 12V refrigerator | 40–80W |
| Coffee maker | 800–1,500W |
| Microwave | 1,000–1,500W |
| Window AC | 900–1,500W |
| RV rooftop AC | Often substantially higher at startup |

A 2kWh power station is excellent for everyday RV essentials, but don't assume it will run rooftop air conditioning for hours.

Also, a refrigerator running on propane can save a tremendous amount of battery capacity. <Cite refs={["turn796730view0"]}/>

For most RV owners, I'd recommend a **2,000Wh LiFePO4 portable power station with at least a 2,000–2,400W inverter and a built-in TT-30 RV outlet.**
